notes: A vector carrying a `canonical` string is a LITERAL vector: it pins the digest FORM (SHA-256 over canonical bytes, lowercase bare hex) but does NOT exercise either canonicalizer, because the bytes reach it already canonicalized.

A vector carrying an `input` object is an OBJECT-INPUT vector: an implementation canonicalizes `input` under `hashedFields` with its own serializer and must reproduce `expectedCanonical` before hashing. Only this kind can catch a canonicalizer that departs from the rules.

vectors.note: Literal vector — digest form only; never reaches a canonicalizer. See I04.

Object-input vector. Every implementation runs its OWN canonicalizer over `input` under `hashedFields` and must reproduce `expectedCanonical` byte-for-byte before hashing, so a canonicalizer divergence fails HERE and not only in the canonical corpus. It deliberately loads every rule the integrity digest depends on: hashed-field selection and re-sort (`hashedFields` is supplied unsorted and names `missing_from_input`, absent from `input`, which must serialize as null); an explicit null that must survive as null; string escaping for quote, newline, tab and a U+0001 control char; non-ASCII passthrough (U+00E9) with no \u escaping; UTF-16 key ordering across a BMP fullwidth key (U+FF01) and an astral key (U+1F600); exponent-form numbers at both ends (1e-7, 1e+21); and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER rendered without an exponent.

Object-input vector over a whole v1.0 payload whose signoffExpectation is the session form (Record §6.1). `hashedFields` is the v1.0 hashed field set: `schemaVersion` is in `input` and not hashed, and signoffExpectation's members are supplied out of order and must be sorted.

Object-input vector over a v1.0 payload with no signoffExpectation key. Under the v1.0 hashed field set the absent key serializes as null (Record §4.2), so this digest is NOT the one a record carries whose digest was computed without the field: such a record reads digest_mismatch.
